title: Not for Profit Salary Sacrifice: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual pay with a 38-hour week, including tax, super, and not for profit salary sacrifice options.
salarySummary: Based on a 38-hour week, your annual salary is approximately your hourly rate multiplied by 1,976 hours.

faqs.q: How does not for profit salary sacrifice affect my take-home pay?
faqs.a: Not for profit salary sacrifice allows you to pay for certain benefits (like rent or mortgage) from pre-tax salary, reducing your taxable income. This can increase your take-home pay, but it affects your super guarantee and other entitlements. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for details.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and an award rate?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026) is the legal minimum for all employees not covered by an award. Award rates are higher minimums set by the Fair Work Commission for specific industries or roles, and may include penalty rates or allowances. Check your [pay guides](/blog) for your award.

faqs.q: How is casual loading calculated and is it included in my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. When using the [timesheet](/) you enter your base rate, then check the casual loading box to add 25% automatically. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

Whether you're negotiating a salary offer or checking your current pay, understanding how your hourly rate translates to annual earnings is essential. The basic formula is straightforward: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. For a full‑time employee working the standard 38‑hour week, that's **hourly rate × 38 × 52 = annual gross pay**. This calculation assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

### The National Minimum Wage vs. Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage (NMW) set by the Fair Work Commission is **$26.44 per hour**, or **$1,004.90 per week** for 38 hours. If you're covered by an award, your minimum rate is likely higher. Award rates are industry‑ or occupation‑specific and include classifications, penalty rates, and allowances. Always check your [pay guides](/blog) to confirm your correct minimum. The NMW applies only if no award covers you.

If you're a casual employee, you're entitled to a **25% casual loading** on top of the base rate. For the NMW, that's **$33.05 per hour**. When using the [timesheet](/) (our home page), enter your base hourly rate and then tick the casual loading checkbox – never type a rate that already includes the loading.

### Fortnightly Pay and Superannuation

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly pay by two. For example, at the NMW: $1,004.90 × 2 = **$2,009.80 per fortnight**. This can help you budget between pay cycles.

**Superannuation** is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee is **12%** of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of **$270,830** (2026–27). If your annual salary exceeds that cap, super stops at the cap. For most workers, super is an additional benefit – it's not deducted from your hourly rate. Use our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page to see how salary sacrifice interacts with super.

### Not for Profit Salary Sacrifice

If you work for a not‑for‑profit organisation, you may be able to **salary sacrifice** part of your pre‑tax income for benefits such as mortgage payments, rent, or living expenses. This reduces your taxable income, potentially lowering the tax you pay and increasing your take‑home pay. However, salary sacrifice can affect your super guarantee (since it reduces ordinary earnings) and other entitlements. When converting your hourly rate to annual pay, remember that salary sacrifice is not included in the basic formula – it's an arrangement you negotiate with your employer. For more details, see our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Your annual gross pay is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For the **2026–27** financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- **Nil** on the first $18,200
- **15%** on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- **30%** on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- **37%** on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- **45%** on income above $190,000

Plus a **2% Medicare levy** (generally). The Medicare levy reduction thresholds for singles are based on the 2025–26 figures (not yet updated for 2026–27 in this estimate). No HELP or Medicare levy surcharge is deducted here.

### Example: From Hourly Rate to Annual and Fortnightly

Let's say you earn **$30 per hour** as a full‑time permanent employee (38 hours/week).

- **Annual gross**: $30 × 38 × 52 = **$59,280**
- **Fortnightly gross**: ($30 × 38) × 2 = **$2,280**
- **Super (12%)**: $59,280 × 0.12 = **$7,113.60** paid on top
- **Estimated tax (2026–27)**: About $9,217 (using the tax scale and $18,200 tax‑free threshold) plus Medicare levy of $1,185.60 (2% of $59,280).
- **Estimated net annual**: $59,280 – $9,217 – $1,185.60 = **$48,877.40** (before any salary sacrifice).

If you were a casual at $30 base plus 25% loading = $37.50/hour, your annual would be $37.50 × 38 × 52 = **$74,100**.

### Important Notes

- The formula assumes you work 52 weeks a year. If you take unpaid leave, your actual annual pay will be lower.
- Award rates may include penalty rates for weekends or nights – these are not reflected in the basic conversion.
- The [reference tables](/data) on our site provide more detailed breakdowns for different pay periods.
- This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax. Always consult your employer or a tax professional for your specific situation.

### Using the Timesheet

To quickly convert your hourly rate, visit our [the timesheet](/) page. Enter your base hourly rate, select your hours per week (default 38), and check the casual loading box if applicable. The tool will show your annual, fortnightly, and weekly gross pay, plus estimated tax and super. It's a handy way to compare a salary offer with your current hourly rate.

Remember: **not for profit salary sacrifice** can change your tax outcome significantly. If you're eligible, factor that into your calculations using our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) estimator.

### Summary

- **Annual gross** = hourly rate × hours per week × 52
- **Fortnightly gross** = weekly pay × 2
- **Super** is 12% on top, up to the cap
- **Casual loading** is 25% on top of the base rate
- **Not for profit salary sacrifice** reduces taxable income
- Use the [timesheet](/) for quick conversions

Always check your award or agreement for your correct minimum rate. The National Minimum Wage is a floor, not a target.
